Technology stocks were little changed in recent trading, with shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing less than 0.1% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising almost 0.1%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Hanwha Q CELLS Co Ltd ( HQCL ) has given up its slim gain in recent trading and was retracing a portion of a nearly 1% decline earlier in the session that followed the South Korean manufacturer of solar-power modules reporting Q2 revenue exceeding Wall Street expectations and projecting Q3 revenue topping analyst estimates. Revenue totaled $518.4 million during the three months ended June 30, down from $577.7 million during the same quarter last year but still beating the Capital IQ consenus by around $18.1 million. The company sees Q3 revenue in range of $590 million to $610 million, surpassing the analyst mean by at least $20.1 million. It also recorded a Q2 net loss of $0.50 per American depositary share compared with a $0.22 per ADS profit during the year-ago period and missing the Street view looking for a $0.11 per share in net income.
In other sector news:
- JinkoSolar Holding Company ( JKS ) slumped Monday, at one point sinking over 20%, after the photovoltaic products company reported a hefty drop in Q2 revenue compared with year-ago levels. The company generated RMB6.06 billion, or about $915.9 million, in total revenue during the April-to-June fiscal period, down from RMB7.92 billion in the year-ago quarter but still topping the Capital IQ consensus expecting $909.1 million in quarterly revenue. Excluding one-time items, JinkoSolar also posted non-GAAP net income of RMB2.73, or about $0.41, per American depositary share, improving on an RMB1.91 per ADS adjusted profit during the same quarter last year and beating the $0.33 per ADS analyst mean.
- TiVo ( TIVO ) was lower Monday afternoon, dropping almost 3% in recent trading, after saying Altice's ( USAT ) European corporate cousin in Portugal has renewed its multi-yearintellectual property license with the video-recording company, helping build momentum for its intellectual property portfolio throughout the region.
